Nina (perf): Heads-up — offline replay (trace id t-84321) shows a clear throughput drop after the recent kernel-priority change + KV prefetch tweak. Running the same trace with the previous kernel selector reproduces the old numbers.
Jordan (runtime): dang, that's the combo we were worried about. What magnitude are we seeing?
Nina (perf): ~12% drop in median tokens/sec on the long-tail cohort (seq>512). P95 latency +18%. Perf-bot summary: `replay/2145/t-84321: baseline=120 tok/s, experiment=105 tok/s, p95=340ms->402ms`
Ava (ml): Did the replay include the new token-budget cap for opportunistic batching? That changes batch boundaries and might interact with kernel choice.
Nina (perf): Yes — experiment applied token_budget_target=1.8k and kernel-priority=v2. Baseline was token_budget_target=2.6k + kernel-priority=v1.
Sam (eng): Can you paste the exact config diffs?
Nina (perf): Sure:
```
- token_budget_target: 2600
- kernel_priority: v1
+ token_budget_target: 1800
+ kernel_priority: v2
```
Jordan (runtime): v2 kernel selection prefers tiled matmul paths at shorter sequences; it should be faster for seq<256 but maybe suboptimal when batches coalesce with long KV caches.
Nina (perf): That's the hypothesis. Replay trace shows more KV cache hits under v1 due to different batch formation; v2 created slightly different batching boundaries so many requests fell into smaller batches, hurting throughput on long sequences.
Ava (ml): Do we have per-batch kernel assignment logs for the trace? If we can correlate kernel choice -> batch size -> latency, that'll help.
Nina (perf): Yep, attached in the replay artifact (link): https://replay.artifacts/t-84321/kernel-assign.csv — small sample pasted below:
`batch_id,kernel,avg_seq,batch_size`
`1245,matmul_tiled,640,2`
`1246,gemm_small,128,8`
`1247,matmul_tiled,720,1`

Jordan (runtime): Oof, lots of tiny batches for long sequences (batch_size 1-2) using tiled kernels — that's inefficient. With the larger token_budget we were letting those requests join earlier.
Sam (eng): Could KV prefetch hysteresis be causing earlier eviction so those long requests lose prefix caching and become heavier?
Nina (perf): Replay shows a 22% increase in KV misses for the long-tail cohort under experiment config. Matches your idea.
Ava (ml): Proposed experiments: 1) keep kernel_priority=v2 but revert token_budget_target to 2.6k; 2) keep token_budget_target=1.8k but force kernel_priority to favor v1 for avg_seq>384; 3) A/B using live canary with trace-driven workload selector.
Jordan (runtime): For (2) we can add a lightweight heuristic: if batch_avg_seq > 384 then bias kernel_score += 0.2 for matmul_coarse. It's cheap to test in replay.
Nina (perf): I ran both (1) and (2) in the offline harness: (1) recovers most throughput (only -2% vs baseline), (2) recovers throughput fully but slightly increases latency for short seqs. Full results in artifacts: https://replay.artifacts/t-84321/ab_results.json
DevOps Bot: ci/replay/2145 completed — artifacts uploaded.
Sam (eng): Sounds like the best middle ground is dynamic kernel bias + a slightly higher token budget. Can we simulate token_budget sweep to find knee?
Ava (ml): I'll run a sweep: token_budget_target in [1600, 2000, 2400, 2800] with kernel bias rule on. Will include cohort breakdown (short/medium/long). Expect knee around 2200 based on quick runs.
Jordan (runtime): Also add a microbenchmark to measure kernel dispatch overhead for tiny batches; if dispatch cost is the issue we could add a tiny coalescer for seq>512 to avoid degenerate small batches.
Nina (perf): Agree. I'll schedule a dedicated replay that includes the kernel-dispatch telemetry and KV miss traces. If results look good, we'll propose a canary rollout with 5% traffic and the A/B harness measuring tok/s and p95 per cohort.
Sam (eng): Thanks team. Please post the replay id when ready.
Nina (perf): Created replay job id r-2145-sweep; ETA ~2h. Posting results here when done. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
